findings.text: follow-on: the response-time half is not guarded. I ran this perf test against the base revision f31a38d (which classifies every pointer) with the head test file in a scratch tree and it passed at 0.180 s EXIT=0, so the test cannot fail for the reason the plan's second cause names; the fixture (39 of 40 pointers at phase working, no manifest_path) never reproduces the 6.5-7.7 s live read the plan measured, and the head live read remains 1.839-2.157 s over 8 pointers (final-live-read.log), still over the plan's one second.

follow-on: the pre-spawn label set {"starting", "launching", "launcher", "dispatching"} is inlined here while it is defined once as recovery._PRE_SPAWN_PHASES (reckon/crew/recovery.py:6178); dispatch.py imports that name directly (reckon/crew/dispatch.py:10208). If recovery's set gains or renames a label, this guard silently drifts and a pre-spawn label stops being re-read, which is the stale-phase case the branch exists to prevent.

item_verdicts.diff: commit af7577adc replaces the unconditional crew.classify_pointer(pointer)["phase"] read in _crew_rows with a direct pointer["phase"] read, calling the classifier only when the recorded phase is one of the four pre-spawn labels or empty (reckon/serve.py:740-742); commit 2926da4ed adds the evidence fragment. I confirmed the returned value is unchanged for a post-launch phase: recovery._observed_phase returns the stored phase unchanged for any phase outside _PRE_SPAWN_PHASES (reckon/crew/recovery.py:6247-6248), so the fast path returns exactly what the classifier's "phase" field returned before — a semantics-preserving optimisation.

justifications.durability: the new test drives the real GET /crew HTTP route over a temporary crew home with a pointer that carries a phase and no stream, and asserts the first response's row phase is not idle; the stream-only negative control reddens exactly that assertion, so a future regression to stream-only phase derivation is caught. But the change under review is the fast path, and the perf test does not redden at the base revision (0.180 s at f31a38d), so the optimisation itself is unguarded against regression and the residual live cost is bounded by no test.
justifications.evidence: I independently reproduced the head focused gate at 2926da4e as 7 passed EXIT=0 (40-pointer GET /crew 0.073 s, matching the manifest's 0.083 s) and confirmed the negative control is a genuine falsification (head plus stream-only phase derivation fails the first assertion with 'idle'). Both arms are recorded completed true (5 base failures, all scaffolding git-clone errors in an extracted tree with no Git metadata, and 0 head failures). Weakness: the perf test passes at the base revision (I measured 0.180 s at f31a38d with the head test file in a scratch tree), so no arm or control shows that test failing for the reason it was written.
justifications.fit: the change threads the classifier's own rule into serve.py: it calls classify_pointer only where the answer can still change (the pre-spawn labels) and reads the recorded value otherwise, a clean reuse of the single phase judgement rather than a second phase rule. Two costs: it inlines the four-label pre-spawn set instead of importing recovery._PRE_SPAWN_PHASES as dispatch.py already does, so the two sets can drift; and it leaves the real live cost (still ~2 s) to a follow-on rather than closing the plan's second cause.
justifications.goal_fidelity: the fast path in _crew_rows reads the recorded pointer phase directly for post-launch runs and calls the classifier only for the four pre-spawn labels or an empty phase (reckon/serve.py:740-742), returning the same value recovery._observed_phase gives for those phases, so the row's phase is unchanged while the full classification is skipped — the briefed goal, matching the commit message exactly. The plan's first cause is met; the second cause's literal gate is met but its live cost is not (the live read remains 1.8-2.2 s and the fixture base was already 0.18 s), so §3 is met as written and only partly advanced in substance.
